All three solutions investigate the problem of whether a finite-dimensional partial isometry can have a circular numerical range centered away from the origin ($c \ne 0$). 

By Kippenhahn's theorem on the algebraic boundary of the numerical range, if $W(A) = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z - c| \le r\}$, the boundary circle requires $c$ to be an eigenvalue of $A$ of multiplicity at least 2. In conjunction with structural results on partial isometries and compressions of the shift (due to Gau, Wang, and Wu), a circular numerical range for a partial isometry can only be centered at the origin ($c = 0$). 

Because no such positive integer $n$ exists, the problem specifies returning $0$. Solution 1 correctly concludes that no such matrix exists and gives the correct final answer of $0$.

CHOICE: 1
